summary: A is substantially closer to the frozen contract. It exposes the exact required Upload signature, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption compatibility, and tests multipart encoding and retry with streamed file content. B directly violates several explicit API and scope requirements.
reasons: A adds Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption) exactly as required; B instead introduces FilesUploadOption and therefore does not provide the frozen API signature.

A uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile("file", fileName, content), matching the established helper and required multipart field. B expands that helper and adds association-field machinery explicitly prohibited by the contract.
A keeps existing FilesOption types and option behavior intact. B changes WithFilesRequestOptions' return type and creates a parallel upload option system.

A tests the multipart field, filename, content, validation, and identical replayed bodies using content streamed from an os.File. B has similar core tests but much of its coverage verifies out-of-scope association features instead of the specified API contract.
risks_a: Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and error handling by calling Raw.Do directly instead of routing through Add as explicitly required.
The Raw.Do seekable-reader retry and ownership changes are an unrelated retry-machinery refactor that changes Add and Update behavior despite the scope restriction.
There is no visible test using a reader that returns an error, although helper errors appear to be propagated unchanged.
risks_b: Upload has the wrong public signature: opts ...FilesUploadOption rather than opts ...FilesOption.
It adds association fields and seven new association options despite an explicit prohibition.

It extends multipartbody with duplicate NewFileWithFields machinery instead of simply reusing NewFile for the required single-file upload path—as well as bypassing Add and calling Raw.Do directly rather than centralizing behavior there as required by the frozen contract. It also refactors Raw.Do retry and body-closing semantics outside scope and lacks a visible source-reader error test.
